doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Not wanting to be a rock star; being new and different
summary: Gates imagines being dressed like Aerosmith for a million dollars, and concludes it would not be believable; he follows his heroes' path.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: “Ivy Divy baby, I ain’t playing that. I’m playing me. You know? So it’s hard to be different you know. And you know I’m not saying it’s hard to be different because I’m different, I don’t think I am. I am not innovating. I’m following in the steps of some people that I dug. I’m not even trying to be a torch bearer or any of that other stuff. I just happen to like the music that I sing. I like that music. I don’t know if — I mean you never know, you never know until it happens, but if somebody came up to me and said, “Listen baby, we’re going to dress you up like Aerosmith and we want you to do music like that. We’re going to get you three guitars, a couple of electric basses, some big speakers, and we’ll get you a wig because we know you can’t grow any more hair, and we’re going to dress you up wild baby. You’re going to look like Jimi Hendrix.” You know I saw Jimi Hendrix live, I dug what he was doing. But that’s not what I want to do. Now I don’t think I could pull it off and be believable anyway, even if they said, “Listen, we’re going to give you a million dollars.” Well guess what. You just hit my number. I’ll do it baby. Whatever you want I’ll do it. I’ll dress up like a girl, I’ll do whatever you want to do. A million dollars? But nobody would believe it. They’d say, “He’s awful.” This isn’t the truth. He can’t sing “I Can’t Get No Satisfaction” and be believable, because he’s faking it, he’s fronting. Maybe I should do that you know. If you know anybody that wants that and they’ve got like seven figures, let me know. I’ll try it.

But you know, I mean I’m making fun, but that wouldn’t work either because that’s been done. You know you can’t do Mick Jagger. Mick Jagger is doing Mick Jagger. You can’t do Aerosmith because Aerosmith is doing it. You’ve got to be new and different. And when you’re new and different then you risk being shut out if you’re too different. Like how did Kiss make it. How did they dress up in those costumes and they made it. I mean they were huge. Somebody had to have a good idea. And then somebody had to make it happen. Listen we’ve got some connections and we’re going to put you here, there and everywhere, and we’re going to put you in print and we’re going to put you on video and we’re going to put you on MTV or whatever you want to call it, and we’re going to make you happen. There are certain restaurants that have like over eight billion sold but is that the best place to eat? Probably not. Cause if you tell me about a really great restaurant somewhere and we go, I bet you there’s no sign over the top that says over eight billion served. Cause it’s hip and inside and only some people go to it, and it might even be expensive. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
